scores.notes: Left Watson is stout and broad-faced with dark brown hair and a walrus moustache; the right shows two candidate Watsons at the door who differ from each other - a slim sandy-haired man Holmes pulls in by the arm (would conflict) and a stout dark-moustached man in a bowler with a doctor's bag (would match) - so the subject is not singled out.

Holmes in both is a gaunt clean-shaven man with dark slicked-back hair, high forehead, hooked nose and hollow cheeks in a dark frock coat and high collar (left in the armchair, right foreground on the street).

Both are night scenes of flat hedged English countryside with a fire sending up a tall smoke column among trees; the left shows it only as a distant glow from the station while the right shows the white gabled house ablaze up close, with nothing conflicting.

Watson on the left (standing, arms folded) has brown side-parted hair, a brown moustache and a ruddy face; the man on the bed on the right has the same brown hair, moustache, ruddy skin and dark waistcoat, though his forearm covers his eyes.

Left Holmes (at the door) is markedly balding with a bare high crown and thin dark hair at the sides; right Holmes (tossing the paper ball) has a full head of thick dark swept-back hair and sideburns and looks younger.

Left Watson (on the bed) has dark brown hair and a dark moustache; the right shows two candidate Watsons at the door who differ from each other - a slim sandy-haired man Holmes pulls in by the arm, and a stouter dark-moustached man in a bowler with a doctor's bag - so the subject is not singled out.

Both are night scenes of a white multi-storey country house with red-tiled roof and tall chimneys ablaze, horse-drawn red fire engines on the lawn in front, bare trees and hedged lanes around; the facade is longer on the left and boxier on the right but compatible from a different angle.

Watson is the moustached man in a bowler on the pavement (left, small) and the standing man with arms folded (right); both have a thick brown moustache, ruddy broad face and stocky build, with hair hidden by the hat on the left.

Holmes on the left (the man at the door pulling the moustached visitor in) is a young man with a full head of tousled dark curly hair and a soft face; on the right he is a much older gaunt man with slicked-back receding hair and a lined hawkish face.
Holmes is the man raising the cane (left) and the man tossing the paper ball (right); both lean, pale, clean-shaven with dark slicked-back hair, high forehead and sharp nose, similar age.

Holmes ringing/striking at the bell-pull (left) and holding pipe and lens (right) is the same gaunt, clean-shaven middle-aged man with dark swept-back hair, high forehead, hooked nose and hollow cheeks.

Both are night views of flat hedged farmland with scattered trees under a dark sky lit by a fire with a rising smoke column; left is close to the blazing white house, right sees the same blaze from the station behind a clump of trees, a compatible distant viewpoint.

Holmes on the left (man at the door pulling the moustached visitor in) is young with a full mop of tousled dark curls and a smooth face; on the right he is a gaunt, lined, much older man with thin swept-back greying-dark hair.

The left image has two candidate Watsons: the slim sandy-haired moustached man being pulled through the door (which the passage implies) and a stockier dark-moustached man in a bowler carrying a doctor's bag. The bowler man matches the right Watson (bowler, dark moustache, stocky, bag) while the pulled man is slimmer and fairer, so the description does not single out one figure.

Left Holmes (striking with the cane) has a full head of slicked-back dark hair; right Holmes (thin man at the door) is clearly balding with a bare crown and high domed forehead, a conflicting hair cue despite similar gaunt build.

Watson in both is a sturdy fair-skinned middle-aged man with brown hair and a full brown moustache; the left moustache has slightly upturned tips and he looks a little younger, but no clear identity cue conflicts.

Taking Watson on the left as the man Holmes pulls by the arm (sandy-brown hair, moustache, brown suit), he matches the right Watson (brown hair, moustache, brown tweed suit, similar age); note the left also has a second moustached man in a bowler with a bag, which makes the pick less certain.
Watson in both is a middle-aged fair-skinned man with side-parted brown hair and a full brown moustache, similar sturdy build (seated in profile left, arms crossed right).
Watson in both has side-parted brown hair, a brown moustache, fair skin and a similar age and build; his hand shades his eyes on the left but hair and moustache are clear.

Left Holmes is a gaunt older man with slicked-back dark hair and a high receding hairline; right Holmes (pulling the man through the door) is clearly younger with a thick tousled curly mop and a fuller face.

Both are night views of flat open farmland with hedgerows and scattered trees and a fire sending smoke into a dark blue sky; the left sees the blaze from the station far off and the right stands in the grounds of the burning white house, which is compatible.

Left Holmes (dark-coated man pulling Watson through the door) is a youthful man with a tousled wavy dark fringe and soft face; right Holmes in the armchair is a gaunt, older, hawk-nosed man with slicked-back receding hair.

Left Watson (arms folded) is a burly, broad-jawed, ruddy man with a heavy walrus moustache; right Watson in the carriage is a slim, narrow-faced man with a smaller moustache, so build and face shape conflict despite similar brown hair.
Holmes in the armchair (left) and raising the cane (right) share the gaunt hollow-cheeked clean-shaven face, hawk nose and slicked-back dark hair.
Holmes with the magnifying glass (left) and striking the bell-rope (right) both have the gaunt clean-shaven face, hawk nose, high forehead and swept-back dark hair.
Holmes with the pipe outside the shop (left, small) and raising the cane (right) both show a tall thin clean-shaven man with gaunt face and slicked-back dark hair.

Holmes on the left is a gaunt, older, hollow-cheeked man with a high receding hairline and hair slicked flat back; on the right he is a visibly younger, fuller-faced man with thick wavy dark hair falling over the forehead, so hairline and apparent age conflict.

The left shows the white house ablaze with fire engines and rose bushes at night; the right is a night-time station platform where only a distant fiery glow and smoke behind trees is visible, with none of the house or grounds shown to compare.

Watson is the man with a reddish-brown moustache and ruddy face, in a bowler and brown suit with a doctor's bag on the left and bare-headed with auburn-brown hair on the right carriage seat; he looks a little stouter and rounder-faced on the small left figure, but moustache, colouring and age agree.

Holmes striking at the bell-pull (left) and seated in armchair (right): both lean, clean-shaven, gaunt hawk-nosed face, dark swept-back hair with high forehead, similar middle age; right hair slightly fuller but no conflict.

Holmes tossing papers in the carriage (left) has slicked-back dark hair with a high receding forehead and a gaunt middle-aged face; the Holmes pulling Watson through the door (right) has a thick tousled curly mop over the forehead and a noticeably younger, fuller face - hair style and apparent age conflict, though both are clean-shaven and dark-haired.

Holmes raising the cane (left) is gaunt and older with slicked-back dark hair off a high receding forehead and hollow cheeks; Holmes examining the hat (right) has thick wavy dark hair falling forward, a fuller smoother face and looks a decade or more younger. Both are clean-shaven and dark-haired but hair style, face shape and age conflict.

Watson seated on the right of the carriage (left) and the bowler-hatted man with the doctor's bag being pulled into the room (right): both have a full brown walrus moustache, otherwise clean-shaven ruddy square face, stocky build and similar middle age; hat hides most of the hair on the right but nothing conflicts.

Holmes tossing the paper ball (left) and bent over the hat with a lens (right): both gaunt and clean-shaven with a hawk nose, hollow cheeks, swept-back dark hair off a high forehead and similar middle age; right hair reads slightly greyer-brown but the same style and face.

Both show a dark brick-vaulted cellar with a stone-flagged floor stacked with wooden crates and lit only by a lantern; left shows more arches, pillars and barrels, right a single low vault with a doorway, which fits a different viewpoint in the same vault.

Both show a brick barrel-vaulted cellar with a stone-flagged floor, stacks of wooden crates along the walls, an arched passage at the far end and lantern light; left is tinted warmer and right cooler, but vaults, flags, crates and passage are compatible.

Watson has brown hair and a full moustache in both (bowler-hatted man with bag on the left, man lying on the bed on the right); right face is partly covered by his forearm but hair, moustache, age and build match.

Holmes is lean, clean-shaven and dark-haired with hair brushed back and a sharp nose in both; the right face looks older and more gaunt with a higher hairline, but the left is a small upturned profile and no cue clearly conflicts.

Holmes on the left has a thick full head of dark wavy hair falling over his forehead and a younger fuller face; on the right he is markedly balding with a high bare forehead and thin slicked hair and an older gaunt face.

Watson is the stocky man with brown hair and a full brown moustache in both (bowler-hatted on the pavement left, sitting on the bed shading his eyes right); he is small in both but hair, moustache and build agree.

Holmes on the left is an older gaunt man with thin receding slicked-back hair and a high bare forehead; on the right he has a thick full head of wavy dark hair over the forehead and a younger, fuller face.
